patent: Fanuc patent (inventors Kinoshita and Yamashiro), Japanese priority 2009-01-29, filed 2010-01-12, issued 2011-11-01. It concerns the wrist axis of a parallel link robot of the delta class: three base-mounted motors swing arms, and pairs of parallel rods carry a movable section that only translates. That class traces to Reymond Clavel's design (US 4,976,582, granted 1990); the classification and the link are ours, since the patent neither says delta nor cites Clavel. Turning a tool on the movable section needs a separate drive shaft from a motor on the base, and that shaft must change length and angle as the section moves. The patent's background shafts are telescoping or paired bars, with a linear bearing between two universal joints. Here the upper universal joint itself contains the linear bearing, so a one-piece rod slides through it, with stroke limited only when the two joints meet. A second embodiment uses three such drives for a three-axis wrist.

glossary.def: Manipulator whose output is held by several link chains acting side by side, rather than one serial chain of joints.
Parallel robot with three base-mounted arms and parallel rod pairs; the platform translates in three axes without rotating.

Coupling that transmits rotation between shafts at an angle. One joint at an angle gives a fluctuating output speed; a pair with parallel input and output shafts and in-phase yokes cancels it. The patent relies on 18a staying parallel to 44a for equal angular velocity.
Grooved shaft running through a nut with recirculating balls; it slides axially with low friction and transmits torque.
The motor; here a servo motor.
Joint allowing rotation about one axis (a hinge).
The tool on the robot's output, such as a hand or gripper.
